Rashi on Niddah 31a:10:1.hebrew: פוץ מילחא - השלך המלח מן הבשר, ושוב אינו ראוי אלא לכלבים. כך הנשמה היא מלח לגוף לקיימו; כיון שהלכה, אז מסריח הגוף:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:10:1.english: Cast off the salt - Cast off the salt from the meat, and it is no longer fit for anything but dogs. So too, the soul is salt to the body to preserve it; once it departs, then the body rots.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:12:1.hebrew: עולה למעלה - כדתני לעיל, אחרונים דר במדור העליון:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:12:1.english: Ascends upward - As [the baraita] taught earlier: "[During the] last [three months, the fetus] resides in the upper compartment."

Rashi on Niddah 31a:13:1.english: All of them emerge as one kind - The seed of the father and the mother become a single creature.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:14:1.hebrew: צבע - כמה סממנין צריך לצבע שחור: קליפת עץ, וטחינת ריחיים של נפחים, וכמה דברים, וכולן נעשין שחור. ואינו יכול לצובעו ביורה אחת משנים ושלשה גוונים, בשנים ושלשה מקומות:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:14:1.english: A dyer - Several ingredients are needed for black dye: tree bark, grindstone dust of blacksmiths, and several [other] things, and they all become black. And he cannot dye [a garment] in a single cauldron with two or three shades in two or three places.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:14:2.hebrew: כל אחד ואחד עולה למינו - לובן מן האיש, ושחור מן האשה:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:14:2.english: Each and every one emerges as its own kind - The white is from the man, and the black is from the woman.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:15:1.hebrew: כי אנפת בי - מפני שכעסת עלי, אני מודה לך, שלטובתי היה:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:15:1.english: For You were angry with me - Because You were angry with me, I thank You, for it was for my good.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:16:1.hebrew: ישב לו קוץ - ברגלו לאחד מהם, ולא יכול לצאת:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:16:1.english: A thorn lodged in him - In the foot of one of them, and he was unable to set out.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:17:1.hebrew: לבדו - הוא לבדו יודע שהוא נס, אבל בעל הנס אינו מכירו:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:17:1.english: Alone - He alone knows that it is a miracle, but the beneficiary of the miracle does not recognize it.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:1.hebrew: ארחי - תשמיש, כמו דרך גבר בעלמה (משלי ל׳:י״ט):
Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:1.english: My path - [Refers to] intercourse, as in: "The way of a man with a maiden" (Proverbs 30:19).

Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:2.english: And my lying down - [Refers to] sexual intercourse, an expression of "to mate with it" [Leviticus 20:16].

Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:3.hebrew: זרית - ביררת בנפה שקורין וו"ן, כמו (ישעיהו ל) ברחת ובמזרה:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:3.english: You winnowed - You separated with a sieve that is called van [in Old French, a winnowing basket], as in (Isaiah 30): "With shovel and with winnowing fork."

Rashi on Niddah 31a:18:4.english: The clear [part] - Cler in Old French [meaning clear].

Rashi on Niddah 31a:19:1.english: And You winnowed me - [It is] missing an alef, [and is] an expression of winnowing.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:19:2.english: And You girded me - An expression of girding strength around the loins.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:19:3.english: You winnowed me - [You created me] from the select part, and afterward You girded me.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:20:1.english: Their cohabitations - The time of their marital relations.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:22:1.hebrew: הוא - קודשא בריך הוא סייעה, שנטה חמורו של יעקב לאהל לאה, ואותו הלילה של האחרות היה:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:22:1.english: He - The Holy One, Blessed be He, assisted her, in that Jacob's donkey turned toward Leah's tent, and that night belonged to the other [wives].

Rashi on Niddah 31a:24:1.english: And they did not explain - [Namely,] from where do we derive the matter.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:24:2.english: Males to females - [In the verse:] "The sons of Leah."

Rashi on Niddah 31a:24:3.hebrew: נקבות בזכרים - ואת דינה בתו, משום הך דרשה: איש מזריע תחלה יולדת נקבה:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:24:3.english: Females to males - [The verse states:] "And Dinah his daughter," because of that exposition: [If a] man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:8:1.english: On the ninetieth day - At a third of the days [of pregnancy] is its vitality.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:8:2.english: How does he know - Behold, he does not know when she conceived.

Rashi on Niddah 31a:9:2.hebrew: מראה העין - שאע"פ שנבראת העין מן האב והאם, אינו רואה. תדע, שהרי המת יש לו עינים, ויש לו שפתים, ויש לו אזנים, ואינו רואה, ולא שומע, ולא מדבר:
Rashi on Niddah 31a:9:2.english: The sight of the eye - For even though the eye is created from the father and the mother, [a person] does not see. Know [that this is so], for a corpse has eyes, has lips, and has ears, yet does not see, nor hear, nor speak.

Tosafot on Niddah 31a:21:1.hebrew: שתום העין - שתום הוא לשון גילוי ופתיחה, כדמתרגם דשפיר חזי. וכן בלשון משנה במסכת ע"ז (דף סט.), הוי לשון פתיחה: כדי שישתום ויסתום ויגוב. והכא דייק שנסתמה עינו, מדכתיב שתום העין לשון יחיד. והא דכתיב (במדבר כ״ד:ד׳) וגלוי עינים, היינו לפי מה שהיה בתחלה:
Tosafot on Niddah 31a:21:1.english: Whose eye is open - "Shetum" is an expression of uncovering and opening, as the Targum translates: "who sees well." And so too in the language of the Mishnah in tractate Avodah Zarah (69a), it is an expression of opening: "in order that he could unstop [a barrel], seal [it], and [allow it to] dry." And here, [the Gemara] deduces that his eye was closed [i.e., blinded] from the fact that it is written "shetum ha-ayin" in the singular [implying that only one eye was open]. And as for that which is written, "with eyes uncovered" (Numbers 24:4) [in the plural], that was according to what [his condition] had been initially [before he was blinded].
